sentences.text: Saurophaganax is currently classified as incertae sedis, meaning its family placement remains uncertain, although some studies suggest it could be related to Metriacanthosauridae, Allosauria, or Carcharodontosauria.
This large saurischian dinosaur was once thought to be a sauropod, but its exact identity is still debated among scientists.
Very little is known about the behavior of Saurophaganax due to the rarity of its fossil remains.
Studies suggest the taxonomic placement is unstable, with some research linking it to Metriacanthosauridae, Allosauria, or Carcharodontosauria, though it belongs to the parent group Allosauridae.
A 2024 reassessment suggested that the allosaurid specimens previously assigned to Saurophaganax actually belong to a new species of Allosaurus named Allosaurus anax.

Saurophaganax lived in the Late Jurassic, specifically within the Kimmeridgian stage, with some estimates placing its range from 156.3 to 146.8 million years ago and others from 152.21 to 143.1 million years ago.
The Morrison Basin, where fossils were found, stretched from New Mexico to Alberta and Saskatchewan, representing a semiarid region with distinct wet and dry seasons.
